title: Finland's 247 Puppy Livestream Draws Millions
paragraphs: In Finland, millions of people are watching a group of puppies grow up live, 24 hours a day.
The livestream is called "Pentulive," which means "Puppy Live" in Finnish. It is made by Yle, Finland's national broadcaster, and this year is its sixth season.

This year's star is Hilkka, a five-year-old dog of a breed called Lagotto Romagnolo. Hilkka usually works as a school dog, giving emotional support to students. But now, she is on leave to take care of her six puppies, two females and four males, which were born on October 10. The livestream started soon after they were born, and the puppies will stay until they move to new homes in December.

The stream has become extremely popular, both in Finland and around the world. People watch the puppies sleep, eat and play with each other. According to Yle, 1.85 million unique viewers watched it in its first two weeks. That is a huge number in a country with a population of only about 5.7 million.
The puppies do not have official names yet. The public will help choose a list of names. Then, each puppy will "choose" its name by sniffing a closed envelope.

The puppy livestream was started in 2021 by Pirjo Koskinen, a science reporter at Yle, as part of a series about dogs. The idea was to show what happens during a puppy's important first few weeks. Koskinen said the show is all about caring, love and nurturing.
Sonja Mutanen, a researcher at the University of Eastern Finland, said that for many viewers, the livestream is a much-awaited highlight of the dark Finnish winter months.
This type of show is often called "slow TV." The idea was first tried in Norway in 2009, with a seven-hour train journey.
